name: Long Guts
summary: Buy an ITM call and an ITM put in the same expiry -- the inside-out strangle. Economically identical to a long strangle at the mirrored strikes but costs far more in premium and slippage. Mostly a historical curiosity.

legs.strike_rule: ITM call, strike below spot, delta 0.65-0.80.
ITM put, strike above spot (so the two strikes straddle the price from the inside), delta 0.65-0.80.

max_loss: net debit - (put strike - call strike)*100. The intrinsic overlap between the strikes is always recovered, so the true risk is only the extrinsic paid.
breakevens: call strike + total debit per share (upside); put strike - total debit per share (downside)

greeks.theta: negative, but only on the extrinsic portion

when_to_use: Almost never. Put-call parity makes long guts equivalent to a long strangle at the mirror strikes, but you pay two ITM bid/ask spreads and tie up several times the capital. The only defensible reason is a market where the OTM options are illiquid and the ITM ones are not, which does not describe US ETFs.
entry_rules: MARKED AS A BAD IDEA -- included for completeness. Prefer the equivalent long strangle in every realistic case.

If used at all: total extrinsic paid (debit - intrinsic overlap) must be lower than the total premium of the equivalent OTM strangle after slippage. Compute both and only take guts if it wins by >= 5%.
Both legs OI >= 500 and bid/ask <= 8% of mid -- ITM strikes rarely clear this.
Capital check: the debit is large (it contains full intrinsic value). Cap debit at 5% of equity even though the at-risk portion is much smaller.
management_rules: Take profit at +50% of the EXTRINSIC paid, not of total debit -- measuring against total debit makes the target unreachable.
Stop: close when extrinsic paid has decayed by 50%.
Do not leg out; close as a package.
exit_rules: Flat by 15:45 ET on expiration day.

No short legs, so no assignment risk. BUT both legs are ITM by construction and both would be auto-exercised by the OCC at expiry, delivering 100 long shares from the call and 100 short shares from the put per contract. Closing before 15:45 ET is mandatory, not optional.
Close at 21 DTE absent a catalyst.
assignment_risk: No short legs. The real hazard is the reverse: both of your long legs are ITM and would auto-exercise into offsetting stock positions, generating two unwanted equity trades plus commissions and overnight exposure. This structure must be closed before expiry more urgently than almost any other long structure.
buying_power: Full net debit, which is large because it includes intrinsic value on both legs.
liquidity_needs: ITM strikes on both sides; require bid/ask <= 8% of mid or skip. This is usually the reason to reject the trade.
common_mistakes: Using it at all when a strangle is available; measuring profit targets against total debit instead of extrinsic; forgetting that both legs auto-exercise.
zero_dte_notes: Do not use. At 0DTE both legs are nearly pure intrinsic and would auto-exercise into a pair of stock positions.
family: Two-leg verticals and same-expiry two-leg combos (call/put verticals, straddles, strangles, guts, synthetics/risk reversals, ratio verticals and backspreads)
